title: Marketplace Integration Onboarding Playbook
author: Leah Park
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines the product requirements, integration checklist, technical contracts, pricing and telemetry requirements for onboarding third-party model vendors and enterprise customers into the Redwood Inference Marketplace. It is intended for product managers, solutions engineers, partner success, and platform owners executing marketplace integrations.

Goals:
- Enable safe, auditable onboarding of third-party model variants into the Redwood Marketplace within 10 business days.
- Ensure consistent billing, SLA mapping, and telemetry so marketplace usages are traceable and reconcilable with customer invoices.
- Reduce integration rework by providing a standardized API contract and verification checklist.

When to use this playbook:
- New partner model integration (third-party or open-source variant)
- Customer-requested private listing (tenant-visible marketplace)
- Migration of a model from hosted-only to marketplace-distributed SKU

Stakeholders and ownership:
- Product (Marketplace PM): Leah Park — owner for onboarding policy and commercial terms
- Partner Success: Diego Martinez — partner coordination and verification
- Engineering (Marketplace Integrations): Connor Li — API implementation and runtime routing
- Finance & Billing: Aisha Gupta — SKU mapping and invoice reconciliation
- Security & Compliance: Priya Iyer — security review and access controls

Key SLOs and acceptance criteria:
1) Integration cycle time: average <= 10 business days from intake to public listing (measured per cohort).
2) Billing accuracy: metered usage discrepancy < 0.5% monthly for first 3 months.
3) Request-level traceability: every marketplace request must include marketplace_token and partner_id fields and be surfaced in Console traces within 5 minutes.
4) Safety gating: model must pass automated safety checks (toxicity, PII leakage sampling) before canary; manual security sign-off required for restricted verticals.

Prerequisites (before engineering work):
- Signed partner commercial agreement and model licensing (legal).
- Partner-provided container or model artifact and version manifest (sha256 hashes).
- Test prompt set (minimum 100 prompts covering edge cases) and expected behavior notes.
- Billing anchor: proposed SKU price points and settlement terms.
- Compliance requirements (if applicable): data residency, encryption-at-rest, redaction requirements.

Onboarding flow (step-by-step):
1. Intake and Triage (Partner Success)
   - Collect partner onboarding form (use template: marketplace-onboard-intake-v1).
   - Assign integration owner and schedule kickoff (max 3 business days).

2. Commercial & Legal (Finance/Legal)
   - Map partner SKUs to internal SKU IDs (marketplace.sku.<partner>.<tier>).
   - Agree on billing cadence and dispute window.

3. Security & Safety Review
   - Run automated safety suite: profanity, PII detectors, hallucination heuristics.
   - Manual review for regulated verticals; record sign-off in audit log.

4. Technical Integration (Engineering)
   - Deploy variant to staging Marketplace runtime (see technical contract below).
   - Execute integration test suite (see checklist).

5. Canary and Observability
   - Canary to 1–2 pilot customers or internal cohorts for 72 hours.
   - Validate telemetry (billing events, trace ids, latency distributions).

6. Public Listing and Launch
   - Enable listing and update Console model catalog.
   - Notify Partner and Sales. Start revenue share reconciliations.

Technical integration: API & runtime contract
- Required request metadata (all calls to marketplace variants must include):
  - X-Redwood-Marketplace-Token: token assigned per partner / environment
  - partner_id: canonical partner ID (string)
  - variant_id: model variant identifier (e.g., vendor/model:1.2.0)
  - billing_sku: internal SKU string for billing pipeline

- Example generation request (curl):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" \n    -H "X-Redwood-Marketplace-Token: mp_abc123" \n    -d '{"partner_id":"vendor_acme","variant_id":"acme-chat-3b:2027-07-01","billing_sku":"marketplace.sku.acme.standard","input":"Summarize the following..."}'

- Contract guarantees:
  - Marketplace variants must support the standard Redwood inference surface (generate, chat, embeddings) or explicitly declare limited surface in the marketplace manifest.
  - Response headers must include X-Redwood-Trace-ID and X-Redwood-Billing-Event (billing token).
  - Max latency target for marketplace standard tier: p95 < 400ms for short-form generation (<= 128 tokens) under < 70% fleet load. Noncompliant partners enter passive fallback mode.

Integration test checklist (automated where possible):
- Manifest validation: artifact signatures, supported surface, memory profile.
- Security scan: container CVE scan completed, no critical CVEs older than 90 days.
- Safety sample pass: >= 95% pass rate on partner test prompts for policy gating.
- Telemetry smoke: billing event emitted for every test request and visible in Console.
- Backpressure: variant respects server-side MaxTokens, MaxConcurrency headers.
- Fallback behavior: when variant is unhealthy, routing falls back to compatibility variant per routing table.

SKU mapping and pricing guidance:
- Pricing model templates:
  1) Usage-based token pricing (recommended for compute-dense partners): publish price per input+output token and reservation multipliers for reserved capacity.
  2) Subscription + overage: monthly seat or capacity fee + per-token overage. Use for enterprise private listings.
  3) Hybrid fixed-plus-variable: base monthly floor + usage split for marketplace revenue share.
- Example SKU naming convention (internal): marketplace.sku.<vendor>.<tier>.<fidelity>
- Billing hooks: every request must emit a BillingEvent (JSON) to /internal/billing/events with fields: timestamp, trace_id, sku, billed_tokens, partner_id, cost_estimate. (See sample BillingEvent JSON in appendix.)

Observability and telemetry requirements:
- Minimum telemetry fields per request: trace_id, partner_id, variant_id, sku, latency_ms, token_count_in, token_count_out, billing_event_id, safety_score.
- Dashboards to create before public listing:
  - Partner health overview: requests/min, error rate, p50/p95 latency, billing revenue per hour.
  - Safety regressions: monthly false-positive/negative trend for partner test sets.
  - Metering reconciliation: compare billing events to raw request logs for daily variance.

Rollout plan and milestone timeline (typical 2-week cadence):
- Week 0: Intake & legal sign-offs (3 business days)
- Week 1: Staging deployment, safety scans, manifest verification (5 business days)
- Week 2: Canary (72 hours) + telemetry validation; public listing after green (2 business days)

Rollback and emergency procedures:
1. Immediate removal from routing (Engineering): toggle marketplace routing flag for partner to OFF.
2. Billing pause (Finance): disable invoiceable events for partner by setting sku status to suspended.
3. Communication (Partner Success): send incident notification to partner and affected customers with remediation ETA.

Release notes template (appendix — populate per release):
- Release version: marketplace-integ-YYYYMMDD
- Variants added: list
- SKUs enabled: list
- Known limitations: list
- Observability links: Console > Marketplace > Partner > <partner_id>

Appendix A — Sample BillingEvent JSON:
{
  "timestamp": "2027-08-10T15:00:00Z",
  "trace_id": "tr_1234567890abcdef",
  "sku": "marketplace.sku.acme.standard",
  "partner_id": "vendor_acme",
  "billed_tokens": 178,
  "cost_estimate_cents": 65
}

Appendix B — Quick checklist for Partner Success (pre-kickoff):
- Signed agreements present
- Partner artifact & manifest uploaded to internal bucket
- Test prompts uploaded to onboarding workspace
- Initial SKU proposal submitted to Finance

Appendix C — FAQ (short):
Q: What if a partner can't emit billing events?
A: We require partner-side billing hooks for marketplace variants. If partner cannot emit, we provide a thin proxy that enriches requests with billing_event_id but partners must accept proxying terms (adds latency).

Q: Who approves safety sign-off?
A: Safety sign-off is a joint approval from Security & Applied ML Safety (email thread and audit entry required).

Related artifacts and templates (links):
- marketplace-onboard-intake-v1 (form)
- marketplace-manifest-schema-v2 (schema)
- integration-test-suite (automation repo)

Contact and escalation:
- Primary PM: Leah Park (leah@redwood.ai)
- Engineering lead: Connor Li (connor@redwood.ai)
- Partner success: Diego Martinez (diego@redwood.ai)

Notes:
This document is intended to be a living playbook. Product and Engineering will revisit SLOs and checklist items quarterly or after any major marketplace incident. For restricted verticals (healthcare, finance) add extra legal and compliance gating steps and allow 3x the typical onboarding window.
